_comment: Workflows that fire on EVERY merge to main, and the job inside each that has to have really run.
Every entry exists because a run reporting `success` is not evidence that anything happened. A job
gated on an `if` that evaluates false is SKIPPED, and a run whose only meaningful job skipped still
shows a green tick, so a dashboard, a required-check list, and a human scanning Actions all read it
as healthy. In the old monorepo, runtime-deploy was dead for nine days that way and sync-components
for four. runtime-deploy itself is not listed here: it moved to hopmesh/platform with the infra
tree, and platform's own copy of this manifest covers it.
`job` is matched against the job NAME as it appears in the run, not the key in the workflow yaml.
Matrix jobs are never listed: their run names carry the matrix values, so an exact match would
never find them. List a non-matrix job that must have executed for the workflow to have done its
work (for native-artifacts that is the attest job: if the authorize gate skips, everything
downstream of it skips too, which is exactly the green-tick failure mode).
ON max_age_days, AND WHY THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS FILE WAS USELESS. It originally carried 14 days
for runtime-deploy and 120 for bootstrap-apply's apply job, which was picked from how often each job
COULD fire rather than how often it MUST. Checked against real history, both numbers would have sat
green through the incident they were written for: runtime-deploy's outage was nine days, inside 14,
and bootstrap-apply's apply had genuinely run five times on 2026-07-22, twenty-five days before the
break, comfortably inside 120. A window wider than the outage it is meant to catch is decoration.
So the rule now is: only list a job that fires on EVERY merge to main, and set the window to a small
multiple of the merge cadence. This repo merges at least daily (the changelog workflow alone
guarantees it), so three days is roughly three missed merges, which is an anomaly worth failing on
while still surviving a genuinely quiet weekend.

workflows.why: Publishes the live mirrors on every merge to main. It failed on four consecutive daily merges in 2026-08 because two retired components could not export, and it was fixed incidentally by deleting them rather than by anyone noticing the red. hop owns the mirrors now, so this gate belongs here.

workflows.job: Sign and attest native release bundle
workflows.why: Builds and signs the native release bundle on every merge to main; the bundle is what release-tags.yml and the mirrors' release jobs consume. Every job in the workflow hangs off the authorize gate, whose repository check can skip the whole workflow silently, which is exactly the failure mode this manifest exists to catch. It was also roughly a fifth of the old private-repo CI bill, so a quiet death here is the expensive kind.
